notes.title: Update
notes.content:
Greetings Runners,

Happy New year!

We have some exciting (and sad) news!
As mentioned in the comments of our last Devblog, we were struggling to make A Maze-ing Runner interesting enough as a complete game (where completing mazes would be the main activity for players).

However, during our development process, we were increasingly excited about creating a couch multiplayer game (co-op/competetive). Consider it a collection of mini-games that are played together with friends. This game would host amongst the more typical mini games (expected in party games), serious genres such as rpg, shooter, racer, etc. Of course Mazes from A Maze-ing Runner would have a place in this game.

Since we pivoted recently, it is still in its early stages.
We will publish a new steam page when we have a playable demo and will inform you here accordingly. But to get you (hopefully) excited about the game, here are some screenshots/gifs of the development progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/0e4d08984896b54ab17a965eae09264acdd678b4.gif[/img]Early stage of a game where the players have to survive as long as possible while obstacles move towards them. (at this stage the player was still moving on a track).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/561453daad3a7ba00cb966d402bf56a0e3b0e57d.png[/img]A more polished version in a Sci-Fi setting. Players will be able to attack one another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/5e9441545ad608a4837da5f9819664d23192888d.gif[/img]
Test of a blast attack against other players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/64f9c78d70b01b4071fd573cc8c8b179999ed9d5.gif[/img]
Test on spawning enemies around the player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/0b9dd3964c7bc45aaf80d92ca7884461cd627b9a.gif[/img]
Attack test, you can see monsters being defeated.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/1e15df4939133d171fb85e0ec4e393fab5d7f3e6.png[/img]Procedural world generation test.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/9bde12722d14bc422dd0c027a4e96748d99ac3ae.gif[/img]
A test to allow players to select their own character.

We are curious what you think of our choice, and what minigames you might want to see!

Kind regards,

Danahi & Szuryon

notes.title: DevBlog #4
notes.content:
Greetings runners,

[h2]Introduction:[/h2]
Welcome to the fourth DevBlog of [b]A Maze-ing runner[/b]!
It has been a while since #3, in this timeframe we made further improvements to our code base, decided to go for (and implement) a central hub with (branch and) floor selection, and implemented a shop, NPC system and inventory (with potions that provide stat boosts).

[h2]Code refactoring:[/h2]
As mentioned in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2849530/announcements/detail/4169844395571358619]devblog #2[/url], keeping code clean is an important part of remaining agile towards the future. In this iteration we further improved the way a maze is constructed, allowing us to place "templates" which the random algorithm will then build around. In addition, the way the tower structure (including Branches) are stored was further improved. If there is interest, we can delve into some code/technical design choices. So let us know if you would like that :)!

[h2]Current Tower structure:[/h2]
In the  [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2849530/announcements/detail/4205875729079398723]previous devblog[/url] we were considering two alternative approaches in representing the HUB/tower. There is either a central HUB which contains a tool to select a Branch/Floor from a tower layout, or a Branch specific HUB/Floor combination (See the previous blog for visual examples).

After deliberation, we want to achieve two goals with the HUB, it should be a familiar place where you can easily navigate to the service you want to use (shop, floor selection, etc.), and we want the HUB to reflect tower progression. For these reasons we decided on the first option.

A central HUB allows you to get familiar with the layout rather than a branch specific HUB. In addition, if a new Branch (update) leads to new services, these services could be added to the HUB in the form of new rooms. This should lead to a sense of progression and ownership.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/0c28e460f6ecb5936a8ae984141042cd58eb758b.png[/img]
While we leave the complete HUB for a future post, the image above presents a functional work in progress) version of the Floor selection UI. Each Branch has its own colour and around three Floors. Floors are unlocked along the way, and the last floor of a Branch contains a Boss Maze which will have its own challenges.

[h2]Ember and Ale:[/h2]
What is a HUB without some friendly NPCs and shops? Like a Maze without an Exit. So let us introduce your first two friends that will accompany you while you take a well deserved break from all that running!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/8056088f915b97b7617f500148b6df9f980b4913.png[/img]
Meet Ember, your loyal dragon friend. Ember has lived in the Tower long before anyone was aware of its existence. How Ember got here, and how old Ember is, no one knows. However, what is apparent, is that Ember loves to hear of your adventures!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/5f1451cb316725dbb493ad8c458cca5c418eaee1.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/5303ccea8e9b3d7df8a28caeb26ec98a0c5ae95d.gif[/img]
Next up, Ale (looks are subject to change). Hailing from the distant "Roaring Thunder Mountains", Ale is here to help Maze-runners (for the right price that is). Having just arrived himself, it will take some time before he fully sets up shop. Initially you will be able to purchase potions, but give it some time, and Ale will have all sorts of wares, and more.

[h2]Early Access:[/h2]
Our aim was to go into early access in August, but we have come to the realization that our view of "early-access worthiness" is not yet realized. We strive to have the core game implemented before we go into early-access. Therefore, we will determine a new (best estimate) release window in the coming weeks and post an update accordingly. For more information, see our Early Access section (date estimates will update soon).

What do you think of the Early Access concept?

And do you think our pricing approach is reasonable?

What is for you a good definition of Early Access?

Thanks for joining us again for another DevBlog!
See you out there runners!

notes.title: DevBlog #3
notes.content:
Greetings runners,

[h2]Introduction:[/h2]
Welcome to the third DevBlog of [b]A Maze-ing runner[/b]!
It has been a while since #2, (we're trying to find a time-frame that best suits our development speed). This iteration has been in the theme of a world map/HUB (and its editor) and other gameplay mechanics which for now we'll keep a secret.

[h2]To menu or not to menu:[/h2]
To start with a controversial topic. Do you need a main menu (every time) when you enter the game?
Look for instance at Helldivers. After their intro scene, you are directly sent to a HUB which serves as a place to manage your character's progression and start a session. It allows you as player to instantly "get into the action" and has a playful way to access progression related features.

We are thinking of going a similar route. However, on your first startup you may want to change your resolution, tweak controls, etc. So we will let you do that after Save-game creation.

[h2]What is the HUB:[/h2]
That is the question. There are two main routes to take:
[olist]
[*] A central HUB that focuses only on character progression systems with a portal to the "world map(s)"
[*] A merge between the HUB and world map which contains all content of the Branch*
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/e7cb48e25048f17b47ec2831d4bf0647a982982b.png[/img]
A central HUB would mean that as a player your routine of navigating to a specific progression system will be familiar, new area's open up as you progress through the game, so you get a sense of ownership of the HUB. The "world map" (or more accurately different floors of the tower) will be travelled to by a teleporter or elevator, and from there on you select your stage. This means the two areas have their distinct purpose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/a8e5ee25ce43aa4a1786f5f14d0912f732130c1b.png[/img]
Alternatively, The HUB is part of a Branch. Each branch has one "world map/HUB combo" which contains all progression systems together with the stages. This means that the HUB can change themes, while the other option will be more settled in a certain style, with new rooms opening with a possible new theme (and possible refurnishing of existing ones). In addition, the configuration of each map will likely be different per Branch, to keep things fresh. But overall navigation through such maps may not feel as familiar as the other option, and you won't get that sense of ownership, since each Branch has a new map.

Below some example gifs of an ingame view of a possible HUB where the stage selection area would be separate from the HUB:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/09a7f085ea7e24601f5ba5da5f7d1e464cb54d57.gif[/img]

and a possible HUB layout where the HUB and stage selection area are together, seen via the HUB Map editor:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/f4e7f62d87c6e697b8fe027d8fd09c439b7913aa.gif[/img]

[h2]The power of a map editor:[/h2]
The benefit of setting up the map editor with the previously mentioned refactoring, is that the hub map editor was relatively easy to implement. While it is not planned that you as player will have access to the hub editor, it does allow us to quickly prototype and test different configurations of the hub to see what works and what doesn't.

[h2]Thanks[/h2]
Well that is it for this DevBlog. We hope you enjoyed this update!
Which camp do you belong to: To menu/Not to menu?
And would you prefer the HUB and tower map (selecting stages) to be merged, or separated?
Thanks for visiting and (if you haven't already) consider to wishlist our game to receive update notifications and try out our demo.

See you out there runners!

* A Branch is how we intend to split our content, each branch has their own theme and content.

notes.title: DevBlog #2
notes.content:
Greetings runners,

[h2]Introduction:[/h2]
Welcome to the second DevBlog of [b]A Maze-ing runner[/b]!
The last two weeks were focused around improving the code so it is more future proof. However, the map editor received some new features and improved user experience to help creating A Maze-ing mazes!

[h2]Refactoring:[/h2]
As a foundation of A Maze-ing runner's critical gameplay loop has been achieved with the demo, we are cleaning up the code. To get the demo up and running we cut some corners in terms of design that work on the short term, but are not sustainable. In this refactor run, everything related to the world and theme was tackled. A major part of the code base which would not have allowed for different themes or alternative types of maps (for instance a world hub). However, there is little to show without getting into technical details.

[h2]Map Editor:[/h2]
So let's talk map editor instead. The Map editor received a major update on the front of user experience and a random mazes.
 
First, camera movement. The camera can zoom in and out, and move around. to inspect the maze from different perspectives and in more detail.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/5e534df49482a6c0a75c50247ccd067433cc9e08.gif[/img]

Second, tile placement validation. Certain tiles like for instance the moving wall have placement criteria. Pointing the moving wall to the edge or outside the maze is not very useful. So messages are displayed when a constraint is violated. In addition, you can also see how linked tiles (in this case a teleporter and its destination) can be identified by a link id.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/ca5266fc6ace454b3ce758623f3e92a2da8382e3.gif[/img]

Last, two last minute additions. Random mazes and Pathfinding. The map editor now has access to our procedural generator, allowing mazes to be created with a button press!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/5aadb82b239cb0dcf53f7af174d6fa8dd466d79b.gif[/img]
And pathfind allows you to see if the maze can be completed (and/or what the shortest path is, fulfilling the completion criteria such as pressure plates and gates).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/3a6f23bba172503c9c901d213d8463c98a709071.gif[/img]

[h2]Thanks[/h2]
Well that is it for this DevBlog. We hope you enjoyed this update! Let us know what you think in the comments. Thanks for visiting and (if you haven't already) consider to wishlist our game to receive update notifications and try out our demo.

See you out there runners!

notes.title: DevBlog #1
notes.content:
Greetings runners,

[h2]Introduction:[/h2]
Welcome to the first DevBlog of [b]A Maze-ing runner[/b]!
Here we will give regular updates on development of our game. The topics may vary from gameplay mechanics to lore and much more! Join us on the trails! And feel free to request specific topics for future updates.

[h2]Foundation:[/h2]
As the foundation of our gameplay has been achieved with our Demo, we are reaching the point where we are working out the world structure. As a runner you have entered the Tower of A maze-ing-ness. In your travels through the tower, you will explore a variety of settings, each with their own unique challenges and rewards! More on this in a future update.

[h2]Map Editor:[/h2]
To facilitate the process of creating a world and the various stages/mazes it contains, we are working on a map editor. While we initially generate mazes via a procedural system (only), we want to have more control to make adjustments. At this moment the map editor can generate mazes with the procedural system in place, or an empty map and make changes to the map (see animation below). The intention is that when we start Early Access, we provide these tools to you to make your own creations and share them with other A maze-ing runners out there!

Currently the editor supports adding, removing and replacing of tiles. In addition you can save and load maps. However, more features are planned.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44920942/b41f50e1d2c0cc8bd2aa07ac2fd22354ca0b3328.gif[/img]

Let us know what you think of the editor. How important is a Map editor for you? Are there any features you might want to have?

[h2]Thanks[/h2]
Thanks for visiting and (if you haven't already) consider to wishlist our game to receive update notifications and trying out our demo.

See you out there runners!
